newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oilseeds markets should eye El Nino, not US soy.
newsitem.headline: Oilseeds markets should eye El Nino, not US soy.

text.p: World oilseeds markets should study the possibly damaging effects of the El Nino weather phenomenon rather than tying themselves to bearish United States soybean weather factors, Oil World newsletter said.
The independent publication said optimistic U.S. yield forecasts which have depressed Chicago futures were premature and ignored the potential for global weather damage.
Oil World said there was a 50 percent chance the U.S., Europe and Africa would be negatively affected by El Nino while there was a 60-80 percent chance of droughts in Oceania and Asia.
This would hit not only oilseeds production, but also grains and palm oil.
Oil World maintained its forecast for 1997/98 world oilseeds production at 276 million tonnes, up from 257 million in 96/97, due to high North American forecasts.
It cut oilseed yield forecasts for Australia, India, Philippines, Indonesia and probably China because of El Nino and trimmed Malaysian palm oil forecasts due to tree stress.
But this was offset by yield forecasts for the U.S. and Canada.

Oil World stressed the forecast was tentative. Ideal weather could bring 1997/98 output of 282 million tonnes while adverse conditions might reduce global output to 263 million. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
